Dear Alice (Chobani advertisement)

A one-minute 2D animated advertisement in which a grandmother’s letter to her granddaughter narrates a future of farms under solar panels and green cities.

Source
The Line: Dear Alice
Creator
The Line, directed by Bjørn-Erik Aschim
Made
June 2021 (The Line)
Style
Solarpunk (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Hopeful, pastoral, sunlit, tender
Evidence
Based on the studio’s project page and the Looper article (2023). The film was not watched and no still was inspected.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The Line, a London animation studio, lists “Dear Alice” for client Chobani: director Bjørn-Erik Aschim, June 2021, length 1:00, music by Joe Hisaishi, art director Antoine Perez, producer Samia Ahmed, animation lead Bishoy Gendi. The studio describes it as “a love letter from a grandmother to a granddaughter and an optimistic vision of the future of farming”. The Line.

Looper says the opening images show sustainable farming combined with modern technology, “such as a cow grazing while solar panels are overhead”, and that the view then pulls out to a city whose buildings incorporate greenery. It says the ad “distills the genre into one minute”. Looper, 15 November 2023.

Joe Hisaishi is known for his scores for Studio Ghibli films, and press coverage compared the ad’s look with Ghibli. Nerdist.

Why it belongs

The ad brought the solarpunk look to a mass audience and fixed its motion grammar: slow pans across fields, wind in grass and leaves, and soft daylight.

It is also a brand film for a food company, so it shows the greenwashing risk that the style’s rules warn about.

Borrow

Use slow camera moves and natural motion (wind, light, grazing animals) in place of fast cuts.

What to review next

  • Watch the film and describe its palette and framing from the video, with a timestamp for each observation.
